subject: The Papyrus · Half of Egypt is younger than 24
html:
A very old civilization, a very young population

Egypt's history runs five thousand years — but its people are strikingly young. The median age is about 24, meaning half the country is younger than that. For comparison, the median age in most of Europe is in the mid-40s. Egypt is, demographically, a nation of young adults and children. (Source: CIA World Factbook estimate.)

The number that surprises economists

Here's a second figure that catches people off guard: Egypt is only about 43% urban — unusually low for a country at its income level. Most of the population still lives in the countryside and the small towns of the Delta and the Valley, not the megacity of Cairo that dominates the world's mental image of Egypt. (Source: World Bank, 2024.)

Put the two together and you get the defining tension of Egypt's century: a huge, young, still-rural population that needs jobs, homes and services fast — the same pressure behind the new cities, the transport lines, the power plants we've written about all year. A “median age” sounds like a dry statistic. It's actually the single number that explains why Egypt builds the way it does. Demographics, as they say, is destiny — and it's queryable.

An ancient land, run by the young. See you next month.
